title: Work from reviewed material
statement: Where reviewed material exists, work from it rather than regenerating it from source notes, since regenerating throws away the review and brings back errors already caught.
detail: An intro-video BrainLift for a Grade 3 reading course starts from the course's existing video scripts, which had been through fact-checking, spoiler sweeps, cultural review and a Grade 3 language pass, because regenerating from the knowledge base discards that work and reintroduces errors already caught once (`downloads/BrainLift - What makes a good intro video.md`, line 269). The walkthrough of a built Grade 3 lesson says most of its content was transferred from the designs, not regenerated (`downloads/SUPERSEDED — see v2.1_ WITW Lesson 1 learning walkthrough v2 (table format).md`, line 9).
against: The same document then compresses the reviewed script, which is cutting approved words, and Split, don't cut found that a cut script lost its style; Remake under new rules asks for a remake when a rule changes, which this rule would resist.

evidence.path: BrainLift - What makes a good intro video.md
evidence.quote: Regenerating from the knowledge base discards all of that and reintroduces errors that were already caught once. Compression is a smaller, safer and more auditable job than generation.
